answer: Because the sonnet cliff is fixed at deposit and recorded in the river ledger, the nectar audit shows how much each key had accrued when it was cut. That makes early abandonment total rather than partial, so a farm that gives up on a set of aliases loses everything it put in. Nothing unlocks before a cliff of 17 epochs, and a slash during the cliff forfeits the entire grant rather than the vested portion. A farm of 206 pays that 28 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
